industry: DTC / catalog / retail consumer products (apparel, footwear, jewelry, bags, home goods, and adjacent product mailers — catch-all, not one trade)
words_and_claims_to_avoid: Fake 'limited time' / fake stock scarcity when inventory and end dates are not real
Inflated 'was/now' or 'compare at' prices that were not bona fide (16 CFR 233)
Bait offers of a product you will not sell in order to switch the buyer (16 CFR 238)
'Free shipping' / 'free gift' that requires undisclosed markups, fees, or hard-to-find conditions (16 CFR 251) — put conditions next to the claim
Invented review counts, star ratings, or testimonials; undisclosed material connections (16 CFR 255)
Unqualified 'Made in USA' unless final assembly/processing and all or virtually all content are U.S. (16 CFR 323)
Vague 'eco-friendly' / 'green' / 'sustainable' without a specific, substantiated benefit (Green Guides, 16 CFR 260)
Continuity/auto-ship claims that hide recurring charges or make cancel hard (ROSCA)
Disease-cure or unsubstantiated health/supplement claims if the SKU goes there (FTC health-products guidance; DSHEA does not soften FTC ad rules)
Government or invoice look-alike mail (39 USC 3001)
A single invented demographic ('all moms 35–44', 'seniors') without list evidence
compliance_notes: FTC Act s.5 + Guides Against Deceptive Pricing (16 CFR 233): former/regular prices must reflect genuine recent selling prices; no fictitious list prices.
Guides Against Bait Advertising (16 CFR 238): do not advertise a deal you will not sell as a lure to upsell something else.
Guide Concerning Use of the Word 'Free' (16 CFR 251): free with purchase means the paid item stays at its regular price (~30 days open selling); disclose all conditions next to the offer.
Endorsement Guides (16 CFR 255): real typical results; disclose material connections; no fake social proof.
Made in USA Labeling Rule (16 CFR 323) and Green Guides (16 CFR 260) if origin or environmental claims appear.

ROSCA (15 USC 8401–8405) and FTC negative-option policy: clear recurring terms, express consent, easy cancel for continuity/subscribe-and-save. Note: the FTC's expanded 2024 Negative Option Rule was vacated in 2025; ROSCA and FTC Act enforcement still apply.
Product safety / performance claims need substantiation before mail drops.

If a card is health/supplement-adjacent (thin in this gold set; beauty and nursing-pump lifestyle appear): structure/function or disease claims need FTC-level competent and reliable scientific evidence — a DSHEA label disclaimer does not cure a deceptive ad.
39 USC 3001: no official-looking notices or fake invoices as 'offers'.
standing_rules: Emotion-agnostic: curiosity, delight, belonging, status, FOMO, relief are all fine when they fit and stay legal.
Every angle and emotion_by_offer combo carries sell_the_outcome_line.
Vendor ROI labeled agency-only unverified; never print as client proof.
Prefer one clear offer + one real product photo + one QR (roofing-round5 directional) unless the client insists on a multi-code grid.
No age/senior/demographic default unless the client's list and offer evidence support it.
Say buyers vary by SKU — do not force one persona.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Deep % off / urgency templates vs brand-first launch cards with no discount
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Client brand position wins: premium launches can keep offer soft; sale brands can lead with %. Compliance still requires honest prices either way.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Vendor ROI anecdotes (PostPilot / Share Local / PostcardMania) vs evidence rules
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Agency-only unverified; do not print as client proof or 'typical results'.
Name the unfinished cart/category; do not imply surveillance or private data the client does not lawfully have.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Invented BOGO/bundle as 'standard DTC' vs thin gold support
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Do not treat BOGO/bundle as dominant; use %/$, free shipping, gift-with-purchase, and launches that gold actually shows.
